pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

Maren Holt and Kofi Mensah opened Teate Clinic in 2014 at 14 Linden Row, Halbrook: a ground-floor room with a step-free entrance, a low couch and a window. Treatment is with the hands, not with machines.

pages.title: First visit
pages.content:
First visit

The first visit is 60 minutes and costs EUR 95: ten minutes of talk, fifteen minutes watching how you move, twenty-five minutes of hands-on treatment and ten minutes for a plan and two or three exercises.

pages.title: Conditions
pages.content:
Conditions

Neck and shoulders from desk work, the lower back, and sport niggles of the knees, ankles, hips and shoulders.

pages.title: Clinicians
pages.content:
Clinicians

Maren Holt (Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) and Kofi Mensah (Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri evenings), with Inès Laurent at the front desk and Ruth Adeyemi as practice manager.

pages.title: Prices
pages.content:
Prices

A first visit is EUR 95 (60 min), a follow-up EUR 70 (40 min), a short follow-up EUR 50 (25 min), a sport check EUR 85 (50 min), five follow-ups EUR 320 and a workplace visit EUR 240 (90 min). Hands only: no machines, no ultrasound, no needles.

pages.title: Stories
pages.content:
Stories

Three people's experiences, not promises: Daniel Okafor, Sofia Brandt and Tomás Rivera.

pages.title: Book a visit
pages.content:
Book a visit

Book online, by phone on +00 44 555 0172, or by email at hello@teate-clinic.example. Inès Laurent books every visit and replies within one working day.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Contact

14 Linden Row, Halbrook. Ground floor, step-free. Phone +00 44 555 0172, email hello@teate-clinic.example. Mon–Fri 08:00–19:30, Sat 08:30–13:00, Sun and public holidays closed.

pages.title: Clinic letter
pages.content:
Clinic letter

Ruth Adeyemi writes the clinic letter each month: one exercise, any change to the hours, and a short note from Maren or Kofi.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Privacy

We keep the details you give us to book and run your visits, and nothing else. Write to hello@teate-clinic.example to see or delete them.

posts.title: Three small changes at a desk that help a stiff neck
posts.excerpt: Maren Holt on a screen at eye level, breaking up the long sit and keeping the elbows close.
posts.content:
A stiff neck at the end of a desk day is usually a story about load, hour after hour. Three small changes help many people, and none of them needs equipment.

Raise the screen until the top third of it is at eye level, so the head is not hanging forward. Break the long sit every 30 to 40 minutes: stand, roll the shoulders back, look at something far away. And keep the elbows close to the keyboard so the shoulders are not carrying the arms.

If the stiffness comes with numbness, night pain or a fever, see a doctor first. Otherwise these changes plus two or three exercises from your visit are the usual start. Maren Holt

posts.title: Building back after a knee niggle: notes for weekend runners
posts.excerpt: Kofi Mensah on slower long runs, one strength session a week and when to see a doctor.
posts.content:
A knee that niggles after a weekend run is rarely a reason to stop training for good. It is a reason to look at how the weeks are arranged.

Build the long run more slowly, add one strength session a week for the hips and thighs, and keep one easy day before and after a hard run. A sport check at the clinic looks at how you run, ride or swim and includes treatment, 50 minutes in all.

We make no promise about a race. We can say what we see and what to try next. If pain wakes you at night or the knee gives way, see a doctor. Kofi Mensah
